==English== {{wp}} ===Pronunciation=== * {{a|en|UK}} ** {{IPA|en|/bləʊ/|a=RP}} ** {{IPA|en|/blaː/|a=Northumbria}} * {{IPA|en|/bloʊ/|a=GA}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-blow.ogg|a=US}} * {{rhymes|en|əʊ|s=1}} ===Etymology 1=== {{etymon|en|id=air|:inh|enm:blowen|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|blowen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|blāwan||to blow, breathe, inflate, sound}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*blāan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*blēaną||to blow}} (compare {{cog|de|blähen}}), from {{der|en|ine-pro|*bʰleh₁-||to swell, blow up}} (compare {{cog|la|flō||to blow}} and {{cog|xcl|բեղուն||fertile}}). ====Verb==== {{en-verb|+|+|blew|n}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To produce an [[air]] [[current]]. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare King Lear|III|ii|296|1|''Lear''. '''Blow''' windes, & crack your cheeks; Rage, '''blow''' / You Cataracts, and Hyrricano's ſpout,}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Tempest|I|i|1|1|Tend to th' Maſters whiſtle: '''Blow''' till thou burſt thy winde, if roome enough.}} #* {{RQ:Walton Compleat Angler|text=Hark how it rains and '''blows'''!}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To propel by an [[air]] [[current]] (or, if under water, a [[water]] current), usually with the mouth. #: {{ux|en|'''Blow''' the dust off that book and open it up.}} #* {{RQ:Tennyson In Memoriam|XV|24|To-night the winds begin to rise
⁠And roar from yonder dropping day:
⁠The last red leaf is whirl’d away,
The rooks are '''blown''' about the skies; […]}} #* {{quote-web |en |date=July 6, 2022 |author=Kim Chae Hwan |title=North Hwanghae Province hit hard by torrential rains |work=w:Daily NK |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20220707152228/https://www.dailynk.com/english/north-hwanghae-province-hit-hard-by-torrential-rains/ |url=https://www.dailynk.com/english/north-hwanghae-province-hit-hard-by-torrential-rains/ |archivedate=July 07, 2022 |text=In Koksan County, strong winds '''blew''' the roofs off homes, while torrential rains poked holes in or collapsed the walls of houses.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To be propelled by an [[air]] [[current]]. #: {{ux|en|The leaves '''blow''' through the streets in the fall.}} #: {{ux|en|What stormy weather —the roofs are '''blow'''ing off!}} # {{lb|en|transitive|figurative}} To direct or move, usually of a person to a particular location. #* {{RQ:Landon Ethel Churchill|page=260|volume=II|passage="This is an unexpected pleasure!" exclaimed he. "What good fortune '''blows''' Lady Marchmont hither?"}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To create or shape by blowing. #: {{co|en|to '''blow''' bubbles}} #: {{co|en|to '''blow''' glass}} #: {{ux|en|Joe puffed on his pipe and '''blew''' a couple of smoke rings.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To force a current of air upon with the mouth, or by other means. #: {{co|en|to '''blow''' the fire}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To clear of contents by forcing air through. #: {{co|en|to '''blow''' an egg}} #: {{co|en|to '''blow''' one’s nose}} #: {{ux|en|The submarine '''blew''' its main ballast tanks.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1983|author={{w|Bill Oddie}}|title=Gone Birding|publisher=Methuen|location=London|page=29|passage=If you've ever smelt bad eggs you'll know it's not a nice experience. '''Blowing''' them is far worse.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To cause to make [[sound#Noun|sound]] by blowing (as a musical instrument). #: {{ux|en|'''Blow''' your horn! That car is about to hit us!}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To make a sound as a result of being blown. #: {{ux|en|In the harbor, the ships’ horns '''blew'''.}} #* {{RQ:Milton Poems|poem=Il Penseroso|page=43|passage=There let the pealing organ '''blow''',}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|of a [[cetacean]]}} To [[exhale]] [[visibly]] through the [[spout]] the [[seawater]] which it has taken in while [[feeding]]. #: {{ux|en|There’s nothing more thrilling to the whale watcher than to see a whale surface and '''blow'''.}} #: {{ux|en|There she '''blows'''! (i.e. “I see a whale spouting!”)}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[burst]] or [[explode]]; to [[occur]] [[suddenly]] #: {{ux|en|Get away from that burning gas tank! It’s about to '''blow'''!}} # {{lb|en|transitive|with "up"|or|with prepositional phrase headed by "to"}} To cause to explode, shatter, or be utterly destroyed. #: {{ux|en|The demolition squad neatly '''blew''' the old hotel up.}} #: {{ux|en|The aerosol can was '''blown''' to bits.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1869|author={{w|Alfred Russel Wallace}}|title={{w|The Malay Archipelago}}|publisher=Macmillan and Co.|year_published=|volume=II|location=London|page=136|passage=He and my other hunter continued to see it two or three times a week, and to hear its peculiar note much oftener, but could never get a specimen, owing to its always frequenting the most dense thorny thickets, where only hasty glimpses of it could be obtained, and at so short a distance that it would be difficult to avoid '''blowing''' the bird to pieces.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|date=2022 January 12|author=Benedict le Vay|title=The heroes of Soham...|journal=w:RAIL|issue=948|page=42|text=However, something once happened on the railway there which showed the very best of mankind: heroism, duty, self-sacrifice and calm professionalism under terrible pressure. It is a story which gives us far, far better reasons for remembering this attractive little town, which without these heroes would have been '''blown''' to smithereens in a gigantic explosion. (Two railwaymen lost their lives in 1944 when a wagon in an ammunition train caught fire and blew up, an even worse disaster was averted however.)}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To cause the sudden destruction of. #: {{ux|en|He '''blew''' the tires and the engine.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|historical|military}} To [[blow from a gun]] {{q|method of executing a person}}. # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To suddenly fail or give way destructively. #: {{ux|en|He tried to sprint, but his ligaments '''blew''' and he was barely able to walk to the finish line.}} # {{lb|en|medical|informal|intransitive}} Of a [[vein]], to suffer a [[rupture]] or [[puncture]] in the wall as a result of an [[injection]] or [[cannula]], causing fluid (blood, medication, or saline) to [[leak]] into the surrounding [[tissue]]. # {{lb|en|ergative|of a [[fuse#Noun|fuse]]}} To [[melt]] away because of [[overcurrent]], creating a [[gap]] in a [[wire]], thus stopping a [[circuit]] from operating. # {{senseid|en|squander}} {{lb|en|transitive|slang}} To recklessly [[squander]]. #: {{ux|en|I managed to '''blow''' $1000 at blackjack in under an hour.}} #: {{ux|en|I '''blew''' $35 thou on a car.}} #: {{ux|en|We '''blew''' an opportunity to get benign corporate sponsorship.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|informal|idiomatic}} To [[fail]] at; to [[mess up]]; to [[make]] a [[mistake]] in. #: {{ux|en|I '''blew''' it and forgot to start the spaghetti, so I had plenty of sauce and no pasta.}} #: {{ux|en|Good luck, and don’t '''blow''' it!}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2006|title=Hating Valentine's Day|author=Allison Rushby |page=148|url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Hating_Valentine_s_Day/XiLirHOQzsoC?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=%22dicking+me+around%22&pg=PT148&printsec=frontcover |passage={{...}} I put myself on the line for you. I told you I wasn't sure if I was ready for a relationship again and you '''blew''' it. You '''blew''' it! You call this a fresh start? This doesn't look like a fresh start to me. You're dicking me around just like the rest of them, Drew.}} #* {{RQ:Guardian|date=20 June 2014|author=Daniel Taylor|title=World Cup 2014: Uruguay sink England as Suárez makes his mark|url=http://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/jun/19/england-uruguay-match-report-group-d |passage=Hodgson’s team attracted a certain amount of sympathy and understanding after the Italy defeat but it was beyond them to play with the same attacking panache and, if there is to be a feat of escapology, it will need an almost implausible combination of results and handouts in the final games of Group D. More realistically, they have '''blown''' it in their first week.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261013065111/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/jun/19/england-uruguay-match-report-group-d|archivedate=13 October 2026}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|stative|slang|sometimes|_|considered|_|vulgar}} To be very [[undesirable]]. #: {{synonyms|en|suck}} #: {{ux|en|This '''blows'''!}} # {{lb|en|transitive|vulgar}} To perform [[oral sex]] on (someone); to [[fellate]]. #: {{syn|en|Thesaurus:perform oral sex}} #: {{ux|en|Who did you have to '''blow''' to get those backstage passes?}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2011|chapter=Chyna|title=How I Escaped a Girl Gang: Rolling in a London Girl Gang |passage=The mandem all used to go round there and get head off her, the sister '''blowing''' the man line by line while her brother shotted downstairs in the stairwell.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|slang}} To [[leave]], especially [[sudden]]ly or in a [[hurry]]. #: {{ux|en|Let’s '''blow''' this joint.}} #* {{quote-song|en|author={{w|Sam Cooke}}|title={{w|Another Saturday Night}}|url=|album={{w|Ain't That Good News}}|artist=|year=1963|text=It's hard on a fella, when he don't know his way around
If I don't find me a honey to help me spend my money
I'm gonna have to '''blow''' this town.}} # {{lb|en|Scientology|intransitive}} To [[leave]] the [[Church of Scientology]] in an unauthorized manner. # {{lb|en|transitive}} To make [[flyblown]]; to defile or spoil, especially with fly eggs. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Antony and Cleopatra|V|ii|365|1|Shall they hoyſt me vp,
And ſhew me to the ſhowting [[varletry|Varlotarie]]
Of cenſuring Rome? Rather a ditch in Egypt,
Be gentle graue vnto me, rather on Nylus mudde
Lay me ſtarke-nak'd, and let the water-Flies
'''Blow''' me into abhorring;}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Tempest|III|i|11|1|''[[w:Ferdinand (The Tempest)|Fer.]]'' I am, in my condition
A Prince (''Miranda'') I do thinke a King
(I would not ſo) and would no more endure
This wodden ſlauerie, then to ſuffer
The [[flesh-fly|fleſh-flie]] '''blow''' my mouth: heare my ſoule ſpeake.}} #* {{RQ:Lindsay Age of Consent|year=1962|page=78|passage=That decision was given an added kick by fury when he found that Podson had left the safe door open, and flies had '''blown''' the meat.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} (of a fly) To [[lay eggs]]; to [[breed]] (in flesh or meat). # {{lb|en|obsolete|transitive}} To spread by report; to publish; to disclose. #* {{RQ:Dryden Fables|chapter=Palamon and Arcite|passage=Through the court his courtesy was '''blown'''.}} # {{lb|en|obsolete|transitive}} To inflate, as with pride; to puff up. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Twelfth Night|II|v|263|2|O peace, now he's deepely in: looke how imagination '''blowes''' him.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[breathe]] hard or quick; to [[pant]]; to [[puff]]. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Merry Wives|III|iii|58|1|''{{abbr|Rob.|Robin}}'' Miſtris ''Ford'', Miſtris ''Ford'': heere's Miſtris ''Page'' at the doore, ſsweating, and '''blowing''', and looking wildely, and would needs ſpeake with you preſently.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To put [[out of breath]]; to cause to blow from [[fatigue]]. # {{senseid|en|brag}} {{lb|en|dated|intransitive}} To [[talk]] loudly; [[boast]]; [[brag]]. #* {{quote-journal|en|date=February 6, 1866|work=Virginia City Territorial Enterprise|title=Remarkable Dream|author=Mark Twain|volume=|number=|passage=I don't want the worst characters in hell to be running after me with friendly messages and little testimonials of admiration for Smythe, and '''blowing''' about his talents, and bragging on him, and belching their villainous fire and brimstone all through the atmosphere and making my place smell worse than a menagerie. }} #* {{quote-book|en|year=a. 1940|author=Mildred Haun|chapter=Shin-Bone Rocks|title=The Hawk's Done Gone|page=218 |passage=He didn't just set around and try to out sweettalk{{sic}} somebody; he got out and out-fit somebody. He wouldn't be '''blowing''' when he told his boys how he fit for the woman he got.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1969|author=Charles Ambrose McCarthy|title=The Great Molly Maguire Hoax|page=113 |passage=At the breaking edge with him and completely fed up with his everlasting bragging and '''blowing''' about his personal exploits, and desirous of putting him somewhere, anywhere, so they wouldn't be continuously annoyed by him, {{...}}}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1976|author=David Toulmin|title=Blown Seed|page=148 |passage=Audie never liked him because he was further in with old Craig than he was, bragging and '''blowing''' about his work and the things he could do, while Audie sat quiet as a mouse listening to his blab.}} # {{lb|en|slang|dated|transitive}} To [[slander]], [[insult]], [[critique]] or [[discredit]] (someone); to [[reprimand]] or [[scold]] (someone). # {{lb|en|UK|slang|archaic|transitive}} To [[expose]], or [[inform on]]. #: {{syn|en|grass up}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1722|author=Daniel Defoe|title=Colonel Jack |passage='As for that,' says Will, 'I could tell it well enough, if I had it, but I must not be seen anywhere among my old acquaintances, for I am '''blown''', and they will all betray me.'}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|slang|informal|AAVE}} To [[sing]]. #: {{ux|en|That girl has a wonderful voice; just listen to her '''blow'''!}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|slang|colloquial}} To [[flatulate]] or [[defecate]]. #: {{ux|en|Uh, oh!
